slides.title: One AI Employee. Every Channel.
slides.content_markdown:
## Voice agents that answer, book, sell and follow up for real businesses

**Phone · WhatsApp · Telegram · Web**

Built on open source, self-hosted voices, and one dashboard for everything. A four-minute pitch.
slides.speaker_notes: This is a pitch for one AI employee that answers every channel of a real business — phone, WhatsApp, Telegram, web. Four minutes. Let's go.

slides.title: Business happens after hours. Staffing doesn't.
slides.content_markdown:
### The 6 PM black hole
Calls after hours hit voicemail. The customer doesn't leave a message — they dial the next clinic on the list.

### Reception is expensive
A human front desk costs thousands every month — and still has lunch breaks, holidays, sick days and burnout.

### Today's bots rent, not own
Hosted voice platforms charge per minute, lock your data in, and still leave bookings, sheets and inboxes scattered.
slides.speaker_notes: Small businesses lose real customers in the hours they can't staff. Human reception is expensive and still goes offline. And today's hosted bots charge rent per minute, lock your data away, and leave bookings scattered. Every missed call is a customer dialing a competitor.

slides.title: One platform. One agent per business. Fully yours.
slides.content_markdown:
**In — any channel:** Phone/SIP · WhatsApp · Telegram · Web voice · Social DMs

**Brain — LLM + tools:** Calendar + invites · Gmail · Google Sheets · CRM/webhooks · follow-ups

**Out — real actions:** events booked, confirmations sent, clean data logged

Pills: self-hosted voices (CosyVoice · Fish Speech · KittenTTS) · one dashboard — calls, transcripts, bookings, costs.
slides.speaker_notes: The idea: one platform, one agent per business. Customers talk on any channel; the agent acts in your real tools — calendar, email, sheets, CRM — with self-hosted voices, and one dashboard showing every call, transcript, booking and cost.

slides.title: The proof: a real call, booked end-to-end
slides.content_markdown:
**The call — Robert × Layla, the AI receptionist**

> "Hello, this is Layla from Downtown Dentist. How may I help you today?"

> "I've been having tooth problems… can you guys help me with that?"

> "Could I start with your full name?" … "robertjohn123 at yahoo dot com — is that correct?"

> "I see openings at 8:00 AM, 11:30 AM, and 2:00 PM."

> "You're all booked in."

**The agent's tool trace, fired live during the call**

`read-back confirm` → `upsert_contact` → `check_availability` → `create_event` → `send_email` → `send_sms`

✅ **Appointment booked** — Dr. Pegel · tomorrow 8:00 AM · email + SMS sent
slides.speaker_notes: This is a real recording, not a script. Watch Layla book an appointment end-to-end: capture contact details, read them back, check availability, book the slot, confirm by email and SMS. A 1:50 highlight of a 5:16 call.

slides.title: Talk in. Action out. Under a second.
slides.content_markdown:
1. Caller speaks
2. **STT** — faster-whisper, streaming transcription
3. **LLM brain + tools** — calls `check_availability()`, `create_event()`, `send_email()`, `update_sheet_row()` mid-sentence
4. **TTS** — CosyVoice, streaming speech
5. Caller hears the reply

Budget: natural voice feel under ~800 ms — streaming STT, fast LLM, streaming TTS. Tuning that budget is the real work.
slides.speaker_notes: Under the hood: speech in, transcribed by faster-whisper; an LLM brain that calls real tools mid-sentence; CosyVoice speaks the reply. The whole loop targets under 800 milliseconds — that latency budget is where the engineering lives.

slides.title: Hire it as a receptionist — or the whole front office.
slides.content_markdown:
**Receptionist** — answers every call on ring 1, greets by name, never puts anyone on hold.

**Appointment scheduler** — offers real openings, books the right doctor, sends invites + reminders.

**Sales person** — qualifies inbound leads, answers product questions, books demos, logs everything.

**Customer care** — order status and common issues on WhatsApp and web; escalates the tricky 5% to humans.

**FAQ support** — prices, hours, insurance, directions — grounded in the business's own documents.

**Info collector** — captures names, contacts and requirements conversationally, writes clean rows to Sheets.
slides.speaker_notes: Same agent, many hats: receptionist, scheduler, sales, customer care, FAQ, info collector. One deployment per business — switch it on per role.

slides.title: $0 in licenses. Every layer swappable.
slides.content_markdown:
| Layer | Picks | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Voice runtime | LiveKit Agents · Pipecat | WebRTC + SIP calls, interruptions, turn detection |
| STT | faster-whisper | self-hosted streaming transcription |
| TTS | CosyVoice · Fish Speech · KittenTTS | swappable behind one interface |
| Tools & glue | n8n · Activepieces · Composio | calendar, Gmail, Sheets with OAuth handled |
| Omnichannel inbox | Chatwoot | official WhatsApp API only — bans are real |
| Data & dashboards | Postgres + Metabase / Grafana | calls, transcripts, outcomes, costs |

Strategy: validate on a hosted platform in days, then move the voice layer to LiveKit/Pipecat and own the margins.
slides.speaker_notes: Every layer is open source and swappable — zero license cost. Validate fast on a hosted platform, then own the voice layer and the margins.

slides.title: One developer. AI-assisted. Real dates.
slides.content_markdown:
**1–2 weeks** — working prototype: one agent, self-hosted TTS, 1–2 tools

**4–8 weeks** — client-ready MVP: phone number, calendar/email/sheets, dashboard

**3–5 months** — multi-client platform: tenant configs, templates, logging, alerts

**days** — each new client after: configuration, not a rewrite

Honest math: AI tooling speeds up CRUD, dashboards and glue ~2–3× — but latency tuning, real-call testing and client conversations take the time they take.
slides.speaker_notes: One AI-assisted developer: prototype in two weeks, first paying client in under two months, a real platform by month five — and every client after that is configuration, not a rewrite.
